exception.reason: UCR supports substantial literary interpretation, stylistics, narrative and film analysis, comparative history, colonial heritage and social inquiry. A complete programme built from these courses would centre on comparative global literature and cultural analysis. It does not sustain the French and Francophone literary and cultural histories, language-specific analysis and advanced French study that together define this target. General postcolonial or language-processing study cannot supply those objects simply by changing the title. The strongest feasible compositions therefore remain adjacent rather than sufficiently close complete responses.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden French Language and Culture combines advanced French with French and Francophone literature, linguistics, cultural history and research. It examines French-speaking societies and cultural expression in France and across the world.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers substantial literary interpretation, stylistics, film study, comparative history and research methods. These form broader literary and cultural programmes, but do not provide the sustained French and Francophone literature, cultural history, language analysis and advanced French study at the centre of this degree. We therefore show Leiden’s curriculum without presenting a UCR composition as a sufficiently close alternative.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC combines 60 EC of first-year study, 35 EC of later common courses, 30 EC of alternating courses taken once across years two and three, three 5-EC seminars, a 10-EC thesis and 30 EC of approved open choice. Two seminars must include research. The alternating courses run every other year; a resit does not provide a new teaching opportunity. Poetry and Theatre requires earlier French literature study and Written Expression; Metamorphoses of the Novel requires the earlier literature courses. Seminar entry requires at least 45 EC of first-year French study. Thesis entry requires the first-year examination, specified research preparation and written-expression requirements; thesis workshop participation is compulsory. Course choices and open space remain subject to university approval and overlap rules.
